text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Belgrade and Podgorica papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA

- The Serbian government has secured 75 million German marks for buyups of wheat, said Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic. Rich wheat crop will satisfy domestic needs, reserves and leave around 300,000 tonnes surplus for export.

- Quality of products and services is a national priority. Only some eighty Yugoslav products have so far received the ISO 9000 standard certificates, said Borislava Jaksic, adviser to the Serbian minister for science and technology.
- Opposition Serbian Renewal Movement will take part in presidential and parliamentary elections in Serbia.

- Election boycott by the Democratic Party, Democratic Party of Serbia and Civic Alliance of Serbia of no importance; Serbian Radical Party (SRS) optimistic about its chances in forthcoming elections, says SRS leader Vojislav Seselj.

- More and more obvious that the new protest by part of the Kragujevac Zastava arms factory's 6,500 workers has "political instructors", says Politika commenting last week's protest by some 700 workers from the plant in Belgrade.
NASA BORBA
- Most Serbian opposition parties disappointed at U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke's appeal to them to participate in Serbian elections on September 21, persist on boycott.

- Results of first round of multi-lateral compensation scheme to clear inter-company debt satisfactory, said Milan Sobota of the central bank's Payments and Accounting Service. Of around 43 billion dinars debt, 5.81 billion or 15.5 percent "cleared".
- Surtax on meat imports are not influencing prices of meat and meat products on the domestic market, said Deputy Yugoslav Agriculture Minister Milan Milanovic.
- Half of Yugoslavia's debt should be written off if the London Club creditors intend to collect even one cent of their loans, according to some foreign analysts.
- Montenegro could independently approach international financial markerts, Nasa Borba quotes unnamed sources close to the Montenegrin government as saying.
BORBA

- Yugoslav industrial output growth of 7.6 percent in January-June compared to the same period 1996 and exports growth of 30 percent highest growth rates in Europe, said Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic. Of 1.5 billion German marks raised from the sale of Serbia's telecom company, half already invested in economic development.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- During sanctions a unique media boom occured in Yugoslavia, resulting in the country today having six news agencies, 450 radio and 120 television stations and 23 daily newspapers, said Yugoslav Information Minister Goran Matic.
- Businessmen dissatisfied with new customs tariffs law. On list of 8,400 products, 65 are free of customs, including lobsters, oysters, snails, coconuts, whale oil and frogs.

- Montenegrin election commission expected to decide today on President Momir Bulatovic's candidacy for president of the republic. Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro (DPS) wing headed by Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic believes the only DPS candidate is Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Socialist Party of Serbia General Secretary Gorica Gajevic says opposition plans to boycott elections hide fear.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Montenegro has invited an international tender for building a hydroelectric power plant system on the Moraca river, Montenegrin Industry, Energy and Mining Minister Miodrag Gomilanovic said. Four power plants planned on the Moraca.

- Montenegrin Property Agency signs agreement with Swiss company under which Montenegro will get a real estate registry of property for its entire territory of 1.365 million hectares by the year 2000. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
